_comment: IAM policy ADDITION for the prod-hygiene-audit OIDC role.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
NOT APPLIED. This is authored-only, like everything else in this lane's
deliverable — an IAM permission grant is a mutating AWS call the same as
any other, and is the founder's to make.
VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-15 (read-only, aws iam get-policy-version on
arn:aws:iam::951921970996:policy/agrisync-prod-audit-readonly, v1): the
role attached to prod-hygiene-audit.yml (agrisync-prod-audit) currently
has RDS + Budgets + Cost Explorer + CloudWatch read + SNS publish only —
ZERO S3 permissions. Section 5 of aws/audit/prod-hygiene-audit.sh (added
alongside this file) will fail its FIRST S3 call (the raw-bucket D9
tripwire) with AccessDenied until this policy is merged in. The script
recognises that specific error by name as the known pre-grant cause: ONE
WARN, skip the rest of section 5, exit 0 — it does not go red weekly for a
cause this file documents (round-2 finding B1). Unreadable for any OTHER
reason (throttle, expired token, wrong region, a renamed bucket) is still
CRITICAL and still fails the run, both before and after this grant lands —
the S3 drift checks are inert (WARN-only) without this grant.
=== ROUND 3 REVIEW FINDING B001 — TEXT CORRECTED 2026-08-15 ===
This paragraph used to end 'but the D9 tripwire's protection against a
genuinely broken read is not weakened.' That was FALSE and has been
deleted. The AccessDenied match is a plain error-string comparison — it
cannot tell 'this grant was never applied' apart from 'this grant WAS
applied and then revoked', 'scoped to the wrong bucket', or 'a bucket
policy Deny added later'. All of those produce the identical WARN + skip
+ exit 0 whether this grant has landed or not — applying this policy does
NOT restore CRIT-on-unreadable for the raw bucket once it is applied and
then broken again. The genuinely unweakened protection is narrower: it is
still CRITICAL for any unreadable cause that does NOT match the
AccessDenied string (throttle, expired token, wrong region, a renamed
bucket), before and after this grant. See
aws/audit/prod-hygiene-audit.sh's WARN text (around 'IF YOU HAVE ALREADY
APPLIED THE S3 READ GRANT') for the operative instruction a founder needs
once this policy is applied.
TO APPLY (founder only — this is an IAM policy VERSION change, so it
must be done via create-policy-version, not put-role-policy, since the
existing policy is a customer-managed policy, not an inline one):
1. Merge this Statement into the existing document (fetch it first):
aws iam get-policy-version \
--policy-arn arn:aws:iam::951921970996:policy/agrisync-prod-audit-readonly \
--version-id v1 --query 'PolicyVersion.Document' --output json > /tmp/current.json
Add this file's Statement entry to /tmp/current.json's Statement array
(do not replace the whole document — the RDS/Budgets/CE/CloudWatch/SNS
statements must stay).
2. aws iam create-policy-version \
--policy-arn arn:aws:iam::951921970996:policy/agrisync-prod-audit-readonly \
--policy-document file:///tmp/current.json --set-as-default
3. (IAM allows max 5 versions per policy — delete an old non-default
version first if this errors with LimitExceeded:
aws iam list-policy-versions --policy-arn ... then
aws iam delete-policy-version --policy-arn ... --version-id vN)
ROLLBACK: aws iam create-policy-version --policy-arn ... --policy-document
file:///tmp/current.json (the pre-merge document saved in step 1)
--set-as-default, or delete this version and set-as-default an earlier one.
Scope: read-only Get*/List* only, on exactly the two buckets this lane's
audit checks (shramsafal-uploads-prod, agrisync-raw-ap-south-1). No
s3:Put*/Delete*/*Policy write actions — this role reports drift, it does
not correct it, per this task's explicit contract.
